meta.title: Velox — High-quality data for robot learning
meta.description: Velox builds a tactile glove and capture system to collect human hand data — touch, video and motion — for robot learning.

hero.headline: High-quality data <accent>for robot learning</accent>
hero.sub: We're building a tactile glove and capture system that records how human hands press, grip and slip — together with video and hand motion.

glovePrototype.title: Glove prototype
glovePrototype.body: Our first glove records five pressure-sensor channels, shown with an estimated hand pose. Signals are uncalibrated (mV).

collectionSoftware.title: Collection software
collectionSoftware.body: Prototype 1 Collector checks devices, runs a capture and reviews each episode. It already replays our real recordings.

captureSystem.title: Capture system
captureSystem.body: One episode combines the glove, a head RGB-D camera and wrist cameras on one timeline. Device-to-device timing is being validated.

wholeHandGlove.title: Whole-hand glove
wholeHandGlove.body: Tactile coverage across fingertips, finger pads and palm, with distributed hand-pose sensing.

fingertipShearSensor.title: Fingertip shear sensor
fingertipShearSensor.body: A fingertip sensor designed to read both pressing force and sideways (shear) force — the signal behind slip.

dataFormat.title: Data format
dataFormat.body: Each episode: RGB + depth, tactile, hand motion, original timestamps per stream, task label. Raw recordings stay unchanged. Training formats (e.g. LeRobot) prepared to the buyer's spec.

whyTouch.title: Why touch matters
whyTouch.lead: Published studies show that adding touch helps robots learn contact-rich tasks.
whyTouch.note: Results from studies by other research groups. They are not Velox results.

matchLighting.claim: Adding touch raised success on a robotic match-lighting task from 20% to 80%.
matchLighting.conditions: Vision only vs vision + touch, pretrained + refined encoders, variable grasp, 20 demonstrations, 3 seeds × 10 rollouts. The robot's own sensors, one task.

touchScale.claim: Mid-training on human vision + touch data raised average robot success from 22.5% to 57.5%.
touchScale.conditions: Same checkpoint, with vs without TouchScale mid-training, 4 tasks, 50 robot demonstrations and 20 trials per task.
touchScale.source: Li et al., TouchScale (2026), arXiv:2610.10288v1, Fig. 5 & Table 4

trace.title: Data you can trace
trace.lead: We build the hardware ourselves, so provenance can be recorded at capture, not added later.

items.cleanRaw: We deliver clean raw data. Irreversible processing waits for the buyer's spec.
items.consent: Every contributor will sign an informed-consent form before recording.
items.ids: Each recording will carry its device ID, consent ID and calibration.
items.noResale: No duplicate resale of exclusive data.

stage.title: Where we are now
stage.next: Calibrate normal and shear response, validate timing across devices, test repeatability, and build the whole-hand glove.

focus.text: Focused the company on tactile data for robot learning.

firstSignals.text: Recorded the first pressure signals from the glove.

firstSession.text: First recording session combining the glove with RGB, depth and wrist cameras.

replay.text: Our collection software replays real recordings.

items.robotics: Robotics teams training manipulation policies that need contact and force, not just video.
items.video: AI video and world-model teams that need realistic hand–object interaction.
items.labs: Research labs in tactile sensing and robot learning — we welcome technical feedback and collaboration.

sell.a: Not yet. We are at the prototype stage, validating our sensors and capture system. Tell us what data you need — it shapes what we collect first.

measure.a: Our current prototype records five pressure channels (uncalibrated). The glove in development is designed to measure pressure and shear across fingertips, finger pads and palm.

episode.a: RGB + depth video, tactile signals, hand motion, original timestamps for each stream and a task label.

formats.a: We keep the raw recording unchanged and prepare a training copy in the format you use, such as LeRobot.

collection.a: By people doing real hand tasks, each with signed consent. Collection sites will be announced when agreed.

research.q: Are the research results on this site yours?
research.a: No. They come from published studies by other groups and show why touch matters.

contact.title: Let's talk
contact.body: Working on robot learning, tactile sensing or hand data? Tell us what data you need.
